basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Separates the abstract legal work from its expressions, language versions and published manifestations.
Keeps norms bound to the exact provision and version that states them, unlike a generic business rule.
Treats a consolidated text as a derived view, never as the authoritative source of law.
Holds the instrument, not the legislative process that produced it or the cases that interpret it.

may: Extract provisions, citations and structure from an authenticated source.
Build a consolidated view and label it as unofficial unless an authority issued it.
Assess applicability to a stated situation and date as a labelled assertion.
Flag conflicting texts or temporal assertions for review.
mustNot: Assert that an instrument is in force, repealed or applicable without a source-qualified basis.
Present its own interpretation as the final or authoritative reading of a norm.
Treat online availability or a formal rule extraction as proof of validity.
Merge different language versions or amendments into one text without lineage.
Retire or overwrite a historic version that past records still cite.
requiresHuman: Recording an amendment, repeal or change of legal status.
Giving legal advice or a final interpretation to an affected person.
Destructive retirement of an instrument or wider disclosure of restricted texts.

considerations: People rely on the stated law to know their rights and duties, so a wrong in-force status can cause real legal harm.
Machine extraction of norms can lose exceptions and conditions that protect vulnerable parties.
Free and accurate access to the law is a public interest that projections should not restrict without basis.
affectedParties: Citizens and organisations bound by the law

items: A legal instrument has an issuing authority, an instrument class, an official citation or identifier and dated versions.
It is easily confused with a draft bill, a guidance note, a court decision or an unofficial consolidation.
Citing a repealed or not yet effective version leads to unlawful decisions.
Translation or OCR errors change the meaning of a provision.
Automated applicability checks miss exceptions and transitional provisions.
ECLI for citing related case law.
FRBR work, expression and manifestation model.
